title: Pindasana
notes: Sarvangasana and Shirshasana are together called viparita karani.
These seven asanas must be practiced in this order, which must never vary: Sarvangasana, Halasana, Karnapidasana, Urdhva Padmasana, Pindasana, Matsyasana, and Uttana Padasana.
After finishing these seven, one should never go on to an asana such as Paschimattanasana; only Matsyasana, Uttana Padasana, and Shirshasana should follow.

sequence.action: Follow the vinyasas of Urdhva Padmasana above through to the 9th vinyasa.

Doing puraka and then rechaka, bring the legs in Padmasana slowly down to the forehead, envelop the thighs with the arms, embrace the Padmasana, hold the wrists tightly, and balance the body on the shoulders only. Stay, slowly doing puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Subsequent vinyasas are as those of Sarvangasana.

benefits: Pindasana purifies the lower abdomen, the spinal column, liver and spleen, and the stomach.

By means of these five asanas, the vishuddhi chakra [throat chakra], heart, lungs, limbs, digestive system, and jathara [stomach] are purified, and perversions of the vital wind, which result in hiccups, dry cough, constipation, and indigestion, as well as high blood pressure, are warded off.
They also prevent illnesses such as asthma, and ailments related to the heart.
benefits_source: The last two are given in the book for all five asanas from Sarvangasana to Pindasana.

verses.sanskrit: Maranam bindu patena jivanam bindu dharanat
verses.translation: The falling of the drop is death, while retaining bindu is life.
verses.source: A scriptural statement, as quoted by Guruji
